title: Her first gramophone and who she listened to
summary: She bought a gramophone in London and played Bing Crosby, Viola McCoy and Edith Wilson, never copying anyone.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: And do you remember -- did you own a phonograph or victrola in those days?
Oh, yes. I bought just a little -- but I didn't buy that until I went to London.

Yeah. I went to London and bought one of those His "Master's Voice". We call it a grammaphone. I bought a little grammaphone. And the old fellow that I know came up to visit -- Al Fair had a friend to come in to visit him. Al Fair just came up to visit Harry and my brother and different ones. And I always believe he stole mine, because somebody broke into my apartment. And I always think Al Fair stole it. I'll always think so. And that's the reason, when Jimmy says, Al Fair says hello, I say, tell him I never want to talk to him. I'll never forgive him. I always believe he stole it. And I'm very psychic.

So I bought this little grammaphone, and I used to play the different records. But I never bothered playing mine. Isn't that funny. You know, I never open my mouth to sing a song. Never. Uh-huh, no. So that's the only grammaphone I had -- record player like, you know. That's the only one I had,

I was listening to other people's songs, like I'd listen to -- let me see, who was I crazy about? Bing Crosby. I bought his first ten cent record. I bought his record. And I bought the -- who was it that sang with Bing when they made a record, 'Count Your Blessings'? Andrews Sisters.

Yeah. Well, I'm trying to think who I was listening to that -- oh, Viola McCoy. I've always listened to her songs, Viola McCoy. And I tried to make comparisons between Bessie -- not Bessie, but who's this girl? Always tried to make a comparison between -- not Viola McCoy -- yeah, Viola McCoy and some other girl was singing the blues at that time. But I never listened to them to copy from them, because I couldn't copy anything from anybody. I've always been individual. Had my own way.

I can't remember now who it was, but I know Viola McCoy was one of them -- and Nina Wilson -- and Edith Wilson. I listened to her all the time. Edith Wilson, Nina Wilson, and there was somebody else's record that I used to listen to. Never trying to copy, just enjoying them, you know.
